Thanks! Is there an estimate for when 3.5.3 is to be released(GA)?

I've taken a look at the code change. While I believe the change will reduce the probability of the bug being hit I don't think it fully resolves the issue. What happens if the selector field is set to null, or closed, by another thread between the null check being performed in register() and the call to selector.wakeup() ?  I think more of the register() code should be synchronized using the same mutex as the code which is closing and setting the value to null. The performance impact should be small as register already needs to acquire that lock when it calls open()

OK. Taking a closer look it seems that you've partially solved the issue by caching the value of selector before doing the null check (neat trick). Unfortunately it doesn't account for what happens when the other thread calls close() while we are working / about to work with the selector.

It doesn't look like it actually caches the value in a local variable. Either way having a null check is simply going to result in register() failing silently and won't defend against the selector being closed by another thread. Without additional synchronization the null check only serves to suppress the exception when the race condition occurs.
@Joe12345 I think you are right... could you please review the latest commit.. Thanks!
@Joe12345 and to answer you question.. 3.5.3.Final should be released today or tomorrow

The synchronized block would need to be expanded all the way up to just before the following line:
Selector selector = start();

Without this wider synchronization block the run() method can close the selector while register is in progress. 

I believe there is also another more subtle race condition present in the run() method. run() performs shutdown if the register queue is empty and selector.keys().isEmpty(). Both of these conditions is true between processRegisterTaskQueue pulling the register task off the queue and actually registering keys with the selector.
@Joe12345 hmm.. I see.. BTW any proposal for a fix as pull requests is welcome ;)
@Joe12345 I think if we put the registerTaskQueue.offer(registerTask); in the synchronized(startStopLock) block also, it should be ok. Don't you think ?

If the run() method closes the selector between Selector selector = start(); and boolean offered = registerTaskQueue.offer(registerTask); it will break. Synchronizing all the way up to above selector = start() solves this.

The race with processRegisterTaskQueue will be trickier to solve.
@Joe12345 to be honest I don't get why there would be still a race.. Can you give some details or explaintation ?
